title: Best FREE 3d model generator to date?
author: WhiteSun1
selftext:
Beside Huan Yuan, is there another option that at least let you export a few models for free per day?

also, best option overall for vegetation and trees?

comments.body: Meshy does this as well you can check that out

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body: Tripo lets you export v2.5 generations for free. You have to select it when you go to generate the model.

replies.author: Snowhhhh
replies.body: I've been using Tripo for a while now, and honestly, I think it's great.

replies.author: Snowhhhh
replies.body: It's really fast at generating models, and the quality is pretty impressive.

comments.author: GreatAdvantage57
comments.body:
I think making a 3d model generator for free completely is a bad decision for a developer or anyone. AI will cost a lot, and it would be needed to be bootstrapped by a creator himself.

searching the cost/quality ratio is much better than a completely free service

replies.author: WhiteSun1
replies.body: Indeed, but they are also greedy

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Most model generation services are a scam. They are designed to appeal to people who have very little knowledge of 3D. 

If you want to make use of 3D gen I would use a local option and then use the model as a kind of 3D reference to model from.

replies.author: WhiteSun1
replies.body: yeah thats what im trying to do, u are 100% right

comments.author: annyin101
comments.body: Even AI tools—whether OpenAI, Gemini, Claude Code, or others—require payment for high-quality performance; after all, these companies are not charities. However, some tools do allow users to get credits upon registration, which can be used to export a limited number of files. In game development, low-poly models are typically used to render vegetation and trees; otherwise, the file sizes would be excessive, negatively impacting both the game's performance fluidity and its overall file size. Furthermore, if you intend to use these models commercially, relying on free versions can expose you to potential risks.

comments.author: Significant_Refuse29
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/c5k8sfcio2oh1.png?width=2460&format=png&auto=webp&s=74c865dd472b89b1a1d6623960a17d1f1907b295

There is also Neural4D [https://www.neural4d.com](https://www.neural4d.com) which is a subscription-tier based 3D modelling and printing service, you can print the figurine and stuff at a low cost. The mesh and quality of texture is amazing, the details are very fine. I used ChatGpt and sometimes use Midjourney to generate prompts and reference images.
